items.title: Thomas Sewell appears in vodcast with notorious US Neo-Nazi James Mason
items.description: The leader of Neo-Nazi group National Socialist Network, Thomas Sewell, has appeared in an interview online alongside notorious US Neo-Nazi James Mason, who is listed as a terrorist entity by the Canadian government.

items.title: $40m bid for airline crackdown as sector warns of higher fares, cancelled flights
items.description: The federal government has announced nearly $40 million to fund an overhaul of aviation consumer rights.

items.title: Labor stalwart slams the 'view from Mar-a-Lago'
items.description: Labor and the Coalition are both acutely mindful of One Nation's rise and its determination to take a decisive role in a future conservative government.

items.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to extend ceasefire despite new strikes
items.description: Israel and Lebanon have agreed to extend a ceasefire and hold new talks on a political settlement, even as Israel carried out new strikes it insists are not subject to the truce.

items.title: Netanyahu's attempts to corral the UAE put Middle East politics on display
items.description: The question for the Gulf states is whether they are happy for Israel to be the dominant player in the Middle East.

items.title: Most widespread May rain in a decade to reach all states
items.description: The most widespread May rain in a decade is about to sweep across Australia as the first north-west cloudband of 2026 becomes a reality.

items.title: Chinese undersea device found near Bali may be part of something bigger
items.description: The discovery of a Chinese undersea monitoring device in a strategic Indonesian waterway last month "shows the extent of both China's reach and its undersea ambitions" and has implications for Australia's defence strategy, say experts.

items.title: Thornier questions lie ahead for antisemitism royal commission
items.description: Jewish Australians told the royal commission that antisemitism has spread into everyday life. But whether the inquiry can handle what it has promised to confront remains to be seen.

items.title: The journey of pollen to a plant in photos
items.description: Have you ever looked at a flower up close?  Or wondered how plants are pollinated? Take a journey through the secret life of plants captured in stunning images by Australian botanists.

items.title: Zelenskyy vows retribution against Russia for missile strike that killed 24
items.description: Russia has unleashed its heaviest bombardment of the Ukrainian capital this year after a US-brokered ceasefire ended.

items.title: Five die following cave diving incident
items.description: The group was exploring a series of underwater caves at a depth of about 50 metres in Vaavu Atoll in the Maldives.

items.title: Jane Caro reckons Australia is kidding itself about private schools
items.description: "There are absolutely no statistics that say that because you sent your kid to a private school they're going to do better in life."

items.title: Scott Morrison joins historic bronze collection in avenue of honour
items.description: A thinner ex-PM cracks jokes as his bust is revealed, making him the 30th Australian leader with a likeness in Ballarat's Prime Ministers Avenue.

items.title: 'Recipe for disaster': Road safety expert 'not surprised' by fatal Qld bus crash
items.description: A retired traffic engineer says Australia is "decades behind" in road safety standards and needs an overhaul after a second fatal bus crash on the same stretch of the Bruce Highway.

items.title: Nic Cage makes the leap to TV in Spider-Man spin off
items.description: Plus, Shaun Micallef dives into Australia's gambling problem and the Stranger Things creators back another sci-fi mystery.

items.title: New Hollywood film excites as Philippine culture hits the big screen
items.description: As animated film Forgotten Island gets ready to hit the big screen later this year, could it signal an end to Filipino typecasting in Hollywood?

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of patron saints, the Friends finale and a 90s club banger
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: Big money and a free degree: Athletes choose US college football over AFL
items.description: A new generation of Australian athletes is skipping the MCG entirely, eyeing US college football scholarships instead of Aussie Rules.

items.title: Swans hold on for gritty victory over Pies, Suns see off Port
items.description: The ladder-leading Sydney Swans scrape past an undermanned but plucky Collingwood side, as Gold Coast defeats Port Adelaide in Darwin.

items.title: Bennett insists Latrell will be fit for Origin despite injury exit in loss to Dolphins
items.description: South Sydney coach Wayne Bennett says he expects Latrell Mitchell to take his place in State of Origin I despite the star centre hobbling off late in the Rabbitohs' Magic Round clash with the Dolphins.

items.title: Natural burials offer families peace at NSW conservation cemetery
items.description: After nearly 10 years getting public health and council approvals, a natural burial ground on the NSW south coast begins letting people have a simpler, more environmentally friendly farewell.

items.title: How the Kimberley's beasts of burden became a 'menace'
items.description: Before roads and vehicles, teams of donkeys used to haul huge loads across remote parts of Western Australia. But the beloved animal became a declared pest that even the meat trade couldn't save.

items.title: Cotton farmer stitches together fashion empire in regional Queensland
items.description: Queensland cotton farmer and entrepreneur Sam Coulton has spent decades diversifying beyond agriculture, building a fashion brand and tourism business in Goondiwindi while creating jobs and investing in the future of his rural town.

items.title: Xi made a historical reference to give Trump a warning. What did it mean?
items.description: The US and China have been rivals for almost 80 years, but when the countries' leaders met in Beijing on Thursday, Xi Jinping made reference to a far more ancient feud.

items.title: As the eldest daughter, I always knew I would care for my parents
items.description: As the eldest daughter in a Vietnamese family, it was an unspoken expectation I would be the one to care for my aging parents.
